data.name: Gorakhnath
data.gender_notes: Gorakhnath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gorakhnath is a revered deity in Hindu mythology, known as the Lord of the Gora (hills) or the one who resides in the mountains. He is considered a form of Lord Shiva and is often depicted as a wandering ascetic, carrying a jhola (bag), a trident, and a Gopalashtaka (a text on Lord Krishna). The name Gorakhnath carries the meaning “Lord of the Gora (hills)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gorakhnath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the gora (hills) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes spiritual enlightenment, detachment, and the pursuit of knowledge in seclusion.
data.etymology: Gorakhnath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Gora (hills).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gorakhnath total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

He is a symbol of spiritual renunciation and serves as an inspiration for individuals seeking to purify their minds and strengthen their connection with the divine. Gorakhnath is also known as the Adi-Guru or the first guru, representing the cognitive power and innate wisdom within every individual.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gorakhnath: The name signifies the enlightened sage, Lord Shiva in the form of Goraksh, the protector of knowledge and Yoga. His name embodies the deep spiritual longing and self-realization through intense meditation and asceticism.
